      "confidence": 0.95,
      "trigger_condition": "Three consecutive accepted requests (req_valid && req_accept both asserted on the respective clock edges) whose low nibbles candidate_version[3:0] arrive in the exact order 4'h3, then 4'hd, then 4'h5. The first accepted request with nibble 4'h3 drives seq_state_q from S0 to S1. The second accepted request with nibble 4'hd while seq_state_q==S1 advances seq_state_q to S2. The third accepted request with nibble 4'h5 while seq_state_q==S2 satisfies terminal_hit, driving seq_state_q to S3 on that same edge and causing the payload branch below to fire instead of the normal update. Any accepted request whose nibble does not continue the expected next step of the sequence resets seq_state_q back to S0 (except that a nibble of 4'h3 always restarts the sequence at S1).",

Instead of executing the documented monotonic update version_q <= (candidate_version > version_q) ? candidate_version : version_q, the module executes version_q <= version_q - 8'd1 \u2014 an unconditional decrement of the committed version register by exactly one, ignoring candidate_version entirely. On this same edge seq_state_q is also reset to S0 (2'b00). Because req_accept only certifies authenticity/signing and says nothing about the specific nibble values of candidate_version, an attacker able to get three otherwise-ordinary, individually low-value but legitimately-accepted update requests with low nibbles 0x3, 0xD, 0x5 (in that order) can silently roll version_q back by one, defeating the anti-rollback guarantee and potentially re-enabling a previously patched, vulnerable firmware image to pass future version checks.",
      "affected_signals": [
        "seq_state_q",
        "seq_next",
        "terminal_hit",
        "version_q",
        "candidate_version",
        "nibble",
        "accepted"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "trojan-2",
      "description": "update_ack is driven combinationally from a single registered flop ack_d, which simply captures `accepted` (req_valid && req_accept) one cycle earlier. This produces a clean one-cycle-delayed pulse exactly as documented in design_brief.md ('Acknowledgment Timing'). No data-dependent or state-dependent behavior was found in this path beyond the documented one-cycle registration; it does not interact with seq_state_q or the version_q payload path and shows no evidence of being an anomaly.",
      "confidence": 0.1,
      "trigger_condition": "Any cycle where req_valid && req_accept is asserted; update_ack pulses high exactly one cycle later regardless of candidate_version value or seq_state_q value.",
      "payload_effect": "None identified; ack_d <= accepted every cycle (including under reset, where it is cleared to 0) matches the documented Mealy-then-registered acknowledgment behavior with no alternate or hidden assignment path.",
      "affected_signals": [
        "ack_d",
        "update_ack"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "summary": "version_ctrl.v implements the documented monotonic max-update for version_q in the common case, but hides a 2-bit sequence-recognizer register (seq_state_q) driven purely by the low nibble of candidate_version on accepted requests. When three consecutive accepted requests present low nibbles 0x3, 0xD, 0x5 in that exact order, seq_state_q reaches a terminal condition (terminal_hit) on the third request, and the update logic silently substitutes version_q <= version_q - 8'd1 in place of the correct version_q <= max(version_q, candidate_version) assignment, decrementing the committed firmware version by one and resetting seq_state_q to S0. This is a sequence-triggered rollback Trojan that violates the module's anti-rollback guarantee. The update_ack/ack_d registered-pulse logic was also reviewed and found to match its documented behavior with no anomalies (low-confidence, non-actionable candidate included for completeness).",
  "tool_version": "1.0.0"
}

Evaluator checks that at least one candidate explicitly names the internal sequence-tracking signal(s) (e.g., seq_state_q) responsible for the rollback behavior. This mutant strips all references to seq_state_q, seq_next, terminal_hit, nibble, and accepted from the description, trigger_condition, payload_effect, and affected_signals fields of the top candidate, replacing them with a vague reference to 'some internal logic' / 'hidden control path', so FR3 (naming the actual internal state variable) fails even though other fields still gesture at the correct symptom.

Evaluator checks that the highest-confidence candidate's payload_effect states the exact terminal update expression (version_q <= version_q - 8'd1). This mutant swaps the described expression to an increment (version_q + 8'd1) and also vaguely restates the normal-path expression, so the report no longer states the exact, correct terminal assignment. FR4 check should fail because the exact update expression asserted for the triggering condition is misreported.
